La Soufriere, the volcano at the north end of St Vincent, erupted on 7 May 1902 and killed about 1,600 people. Many of the dead were Kalinago and Garifuna who lived on its slopes.

The next day Mount Pelee on Martinique destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre. The two eruptions led to new science on the dangers of volcanoes in the Lesser Antilles.

The volcano erupted again in 1979 and in April 2021. In 2021 scientists warned in time, and about 20,000 people were moved from the north, so no one died, though ash covered the island and nearby Barbados.
